🤖 The AI investment race is not only a technology story

It is also a capital-allocation story.

A new BIS working paper models the current AI build-out as a race for a small number of dominant market positions.

The result is uncomfortable.

Under the paper’s conservative baseline, firms overinvest by roughly 50% relative to the socially efficient level. Under weaker demand conditions, that gap can rise to around three times the efficient level.

Why?

Because every company faces the same pressure:

Invest early.
Build capacity first.
Secure the market before someone else does.

That can produce:

• duplicated infrastructure
• debt-funded expansion
• circular financial relationships
• specialised assets that are difficult to resell
• larger losses if revenue expectations fail

The paper does not argue that AI lacks economic value.

It argues that real technological value does not guarantee efficient capital allocation.

A transformative technology can still create an unstable investment cycle.

For markets, the useful question is not only:

“How powerful is the technology?”

It is also:

“How much capital already depends on the most optimistic outcome?”

Capability explains the opportunity.
The balance sheet explains the fragility.

Source: BIS Working Paper No. 1367, The AI Investment Race, 14 July 2026.
